title: A time and Earth-velocity fit gives a -1.36 m/s per year difference between two ESPRESSO reductions of HD 20794
abstract: We compare two public ESPRESSO velocity reductions of HD 20794 for 651 matched spectra on 64 nights. A joint time and Earth-velocity fit gives a DRS-minus-sBART drift of -1.3570 m/s per year. Its conditional 30-day block interval is -1.3799 to -1.3336. Independent Hipparcos astrometry predicts a perspective acceleration of +1.3555 m/s per year. This supports a correction-convention explanation but does not prove the processing history. The Earth-velocity coefficient is -0.01264 m/s per km/s. An alternative one-year sine fit gives a 0.2105 m/s semi-amplitude. The joint fit removes 99.47 percent of difference variance and leaves 0.1018 m/s RMS. With drift fixed from Hipparcos, the Earth-velocity term reduces pooled omitted-season squared error by 58.7 percent. These are retrospective checks. Extra baseline terms move the fitted drift, and residual power remains near the known outer planet period. The reductions share spectra and are not independent confirmation. No new planet or specific hardware fault is found. The bundle contains frozen paired data, source hashes, code, figures, sensitivity fits, and offline reproduction steps.

display.caption: Differences between 651 matched spectra on 64 nights. A time and Earth-velocity fit leaves 0.102 m/s RMS. Hipparcos predicts a drift of similar magnitude. The match supports a convention difference, but does not prove its cause.

Omitted-season prediction errors and exploratory period fits of the reduction difference. The fixed astrometric drift plus Earth velocity has smaller pooled error. Residual long-period power remains; no new object is claimed.
